dispositions.reason: The modern stele directly transmits the chronicle sequence; promotion is limited to the fact of transmission, not ancient-event verification.
The field inscription is sufficient evidence for a transmitted Poson/Ambasthala narrative when bounded as tradition.
The stele supports a foundation/ordination tradition; later epigraphy is kept separate from the ancient narrative.
The bundled Thuparama/Sanghamitta/Bodhi/bhikkhuni sequence is retained explicitly as transmitted tradition.
The inscription supports the commemorative tradition and its chronology convention, not an independent archaeological date.
The 2024 completion date is direct inscriptional evidence; the ~100,000 figure remains attributed to the commissioning text rather than treated as measured attendance.
The superlative is retained only as an attributed statement by the excavation project lead.
The announcement directly supports an analysis/publication intention, not completion of either action.
The press announcement's framing is recordable as source fact while specialist doctrinal closure remains explicitly excluded.
